cases.name: a uuid without dashes is not a uuid
any uuid version and variant is accepted
cases.note: Those bits say who generated it, not whether the value is a UUID.

cases.name: an address with no at-sign is not an email
an email needs a dotted domain
cases.note: A domain with no dot is syntactically fine and never routable from outside its own network, which at an API boundary is a typo every time.

cases.name: a plus tag and subdomains are accepted
cases.note: Rejecting these is the classic over-strict email check, and it lands on a user holding a perfectly good address.

cases.name: a space in the local part is refused
a hostname label may not start or end with a hyphen
an empty hostname label is refused
an octet above 255 is not an ipv4 address
a leading zero in an octet is refused
cases.note: 010 is octal to some resolvers and decimal to others, and a value that means two different things on two hosts is what this project exists to refuse.

cases.name: the ipv6 short form and an embedded ipv4 are accepted
two elisions are not an ipv6 address
an ipv6 zone identifier is refused
cases.note: It names an interface on one machine and means nothing on another.

cases.name: a format and a length bound both apply, in declaration order
a format says nothing about a field that is absent
